title: Outcomes, requests, commitments and forms
description: The shared encodings the resolver writes and institutions read (docs/design/translator-and-resolver.md §9). They live inside records' opaque data, and the kernel never checks them (records are never judged, D22). They are a platform standard, like the message formats banks exchange, so that code participants, language participants and institutions all read and write one language.

Outcome.description: A physical outcome someone is asked or committed to bring about: exactly one key.

goods.description: Goods delivered (phase B): a quantity of a kind to someone at a place, from the one committed's holding (at `from`, if said).

on.description: A lot (a registry record over cells), or a cell: where the builder is to put it.

who.description: A person (whose body goes in or comes out).

in.description: A space (apts-3/dwelling.2), or a building (for leaving it: every space the person is in there).

RequestData.description: The data of a statement of kind 'request': whoever it is addressed to is asked to bring the outcome about, once, or every 'every' seconds. When the first of them falls: on the date 'first_at' (the moment that day begins; never before the day of the request), else 'first' seconds after the request, else one 'every' after it. A request carries 'first_at' or 'first', not both. They decide.

Commitment.description: An agreement commitment's 'does', in the standard encoding: the outcome the party commits to bring about. Free-form terms stay in the agreement's text.

FieldType.description: What a form's field takes. `list`: several ids (a JSON list, or one id). `date`: a day as reports write one ("year 1, day 12", or "day 12" of the first year), read as the moment it begins; or a moment in seconds, as bare digits.

FormWrites.description: How a form that is a paper of an office's own is written from its fields (participants/src/forms.ts; both resolvers, held to contracts/test/forms.json): the statement's kind, its words, its content, whom it is addressed to, who sees it, what it cites, and what it offers or asserts. Each of data, to, visible, offer and assertion is a template: JSON in which a string "=name" is the field as the form reads it (an amount as a decimal string, a length of time or a date in seconds, a count as a number, a list as its ids), "#name" the field as a whole number, "?name" a yes-or-no choice as true or false, "+name" a length of time counted from now, and "=self" whoever the paper is made for. A field not given leaves its key, or its place in a list, out; a list given where one item stands is set out in its place. In `text`, {name} is the field in words. Such a form does not cite itself: `basis` names the field that is the paper's basis, if it has one.

claim.description: A claim the form records beside its paper, in the same act and before it: what a decision grants (a permit's liberty to build), so that a paper that says something is permitted and the record others check are made together. Where `when` holds (each field named has that value; absent: always), `holder` has `position` about `about`, citing `basis`. `holder` and `basis` each name a field ("=applicant"; "=self" for whoever the paper is made for) and `about` is a template as `data` is. Every field they name is then needed, and one not given is asked for; where `when` does not hold, no claim is recorded and those fields may be left empty. A form without it records none.

sends.description: Whom every paper made on the form goes to whatever its fields say (those named in `to` by the form itself, not by a field), and why, in the form's own words: what whoever fills the form in is told of them, on the form and in a draft's preview. Each `to` lists them (in a module's declaration, "@name" for what is the office's own). It changes nothing a paper carries.

FormData.description: The data of a statement of kind 'form': the input an institution expects. Filling it in publishes a statement of kind 'submit_as', addressed to 'submit_to', with the fields as its data, citing the form as its basis.

office.description: The office (a position) whose form it is, where it is one office's and not its whole organisation's: a direction that office takes. A call names such a form's office as its `to`.

writes.description: For a paper of the office's own: how it is written from the fields. Without it, the fields are the statement's data, it is addressed to `submit_to`, and it cites the form.
